ops.text: 13A. Intellectual Property and Data. (a) As between the Parties, Customer exclusively owns and retains all right, title and interest in and to the Content, the Properties, the Requests, and all data and information provided by, or collected from, Customer, the Properties or their visitors in connection with the Services (collectively, "Customer Data"), together with all deliverables and work product prepared for Customer under this Agreement or any Exhibit, and Kubient hereby assigns to Customer all right, title and interest it may have in such deliverables and work product. (b) Kubient retains all right, title and interest in the Auction Platform and its other pre-existing or generally applicable technology, tools and know-how, and to the extent any such Kubient materials are incorporated in a deliverable, Kubient grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, sublicensable license to use, modify and exploit the same as part of that deliverable for Customer's business purposes. (c) Kubient may use Customer Data solely as necessary to provide the Services during the Term, and nothing in this Agreement grants Kubient any ownership of, or joint ownership in, any Customer intellectual property or Customer Data.

quote: (viii) it is the rightful owner or licensee of all intellectual property rights to the Service, the Auction Platform and products delivered hereunder;
rationale: The Agreement contains no IP or data ownership provision. The only proprietary-rights language is a warranty that Kubient owns the IP in the Service, Auction Platform and "products delivered hereunder" (p0040), a trademark/logo carve-out (p0065), and a clause making AP "solely liable" for its Content and the IP rights therein (p0025) without confirming AP owns them. Nothing allocates ownership of deliverables or work product prepared for AP, and nothing addresses AP's data (including Requests sent to Kubient and visitor data Kubient collects and stores under p0035). That leaves the vendor warranty as the only ownership statement touching delivered products and gives AP no licence back to embedded Kubient materials. We therefore added a short IP and data section: AP retains its Content, Properties and data and owns deliverables (Kubient assigns), Kubient keeps the Auction Platform and its pre-existing tools with a perpetual, royalty-free licence back for embedded materials, Kubient's data use is limited to providing the Services, and no joint ownership is created.

quote: This Agreement will automatically renew for additional 1-year terms unless earlier terminated pursuant to this Agreement's express provisions (together with the Initial Term, such additional periods the "Term"). Neither Party may terminate this Agreement during the Initial Term except as set forth in paragraph 4(b) or any Exhibit. Either Party may terminate this Agreement for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other Party.
rationale: Paragraph 4(a) provides indefinite automatic 1-year renewals with no non-renewal mechanism: the only exit is a for-convenience termination on ninety (90) days' written notice available only after the Initial Term, so Customer's effective opt-out window is 90 days — at the walk-away boundary and well beyond the preferred 30 days (fallback 60 days). There is also no vendor renewal reminder. Renewal term length (12 months) is compliant, and the revenue-share fee model in paragraph 5 contains no price-uplift language, so no uplift cap is needed. Redline adds a 30-day Customer non-renewal right and a 60-day Kubient reminder while leaving the existing termination rights untouched.

checks.detail: changed-character ratio=0.550 (advisory: whole-clause rewrites are acceptable when the rule requires them)
checks.name: minimal edit p0016

verification.notes: The deviation is correctly identified: the original clause provides indefinite automatic 1-year renewals with no non-renewal mechanism, leaving a 90-day for-convenience notice (available only after the Initial Term) as the sole exit — at the walk-away boundary and well outside the preferred 30-day / fallback 60-day window, and with no vendor reminder. The redline reaches the preferred position with a targeted insertion: a Customer 30-day non-renewal right into the auto-renewal sentence plus a separate 60-day Kubient renewal reminder, leaving renewal term length (12 months, already compliant) and the parties' existing termination rights intact. The failing deterministic check ('non-renewal notice window ≤ 60 days', value=90) is a false positive: the 90-day figure comes from the untouched mutual for-convenience termination sentence, not the newly added non-renewal window, which is 30 days. The 0.55 changed-character ratio is likewise advisory and overstates the edit, which is two clean insertions into a long paragraph. Omission of a price-uplift cap is justified: the fee model is revenue-share and the cited text contains no uplift language, so no cap is required by the rule. The comment is accurate, correctly states the playbook preferred position and the 60-day fallback, and matches the tone requirements. Minor, non-fatal: the retained sentence 'Neither Party may terminate this Agreement during the Initial Term...' could be read as friction with a non-renewal notice served during the Initial Term; a short carve-out ('other than a notice of non-renewal under this paragraph 4(a)') would remove any ambiguity, but non-renewal is conventionally distinct from termination so the edit remains operative.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We added an orderly exit provision so that, on termination, Kubient gives us up to six months of transition assistance at its then-current rates, returns our data in a machine-readable format within thirty days, and then deletes and certifies deletion. Our playbook requires data return and migration support on exit; we can accept ninety days of transition assistance as a fallback.

ops.text: (v) at Customer's request, Kubient will provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months following such termination or expiration at Kubient's then-current rates; (vi) within thirty (30) days of such termination or expiration, Kubient will return to Customer all Requests, Content and other data of or relating to Customer, its Properties, Inventory or Impressions that is in Kubient's possession or control (collectively, "Customer Data") in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (vii) thereafter Kubient will delete all Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion to Customer in writing.

proposal.summary: Insert transition assistance, data return and deletion certification into termination effects (para 4(c))

rationale: The termination-effects provision (para 4(c)) only requires Kubient to cease the Services, revocation of the license, Customer to stop using the platform, and mutual return/destruction of Confidential Information. There is no obligation on Kubient to provide transition assistance, to return AP's data (Requests, Content and related data) in a usable machine-readable format, or to delete and certify deletion afterwards, and no such language appears elsewhere in the Agreement (no hits for transition, export, migration or Customer Data). For a hosted ad-auction service handling AP data, this absence is a deviation, so we insert the playbook exit provision as new sub-clauses (v)-(vii) of para 4(c): six months' transition assistance at then-current rates, data return within thirty days, then deletion with written certification.
ruleTitle: Post-termination transition assistance and data return

verification.notes: Rule is a 'missing' insert and the record supports it: para 4(c)(i)-(iv) only addresses cessation of Services, license revocation and mutual Confidential Information return/destruction, with no transition assistance, data return or deletion certification anywhere cited. The inserted sub-clauses (v)-(vii) track the playbook model language closely — six (6) months of transition assistance at Kubient's then-current rates, return of Customer Data in a commonly used machine-readable format within thirty (30) days, and subsequent deletion with written certification — reaching the preferred position with a minimal, additive edit. Insertion is correctly located in the termination-effects section, is drafted in the counterparty's own vocabulary (Requests, Content, Properties, Inventory, Impressions) and defines 'Customer Data' inline since the Agreement lacks that term. Comment is accurate, concise, in first person plural with the [Playbook] prefix, explains the change, cites the playbook position and offers the 90-day fallback without lecturing. Minor drafting nit only (clause (iv) begins with 'and', so appending (v)-(vii) after it reads slightly awkwardly); this does not affect enforceability or the substantive position.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We added a professional and workmanlike services warranty plus a conformance warranty with a stated duration (90 days for services, 12 months for software deliverables) and an express re-performance, repair/replacement or refund remedy, because the current warranties in Section 9(b) have no period and no remedy. We can accept a 90-day period for software deliverables if that is a concern.

ops.text: (xii) the Service and any other services provided hereunder will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (xiii) for a period of ninety (90) days following performance (and, in the case of any software deliverable, twelve (12) months following delivery), the services and deliverables provided hereunder will conform in all material respects to their applicable documentation and specifications. Customer's remedy for breach of the warranties in this Section 9(b) is, at Kubient's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming services or deliverable, which remedy is in addition to, and does not limit, Customer's other rights and remedies under this Agreement.

proposal.summary: Add a workmanlike performance warranty, a conformance warranty period and a repair/replace/refund remedy to Kubient's warranties

quote: (ii) the Service will perform in all material respects to industry standards;
rationale: Section 9(b) contains vendor warranties covering non-infringement, security, no malicious code, compliance with Laws and services "free from errors that materially affect their utility", but it omits (i) a professional and workmanlike performance warranty, (ii) any warranty period for conformance of the Service/deliverables to documentation, and (iii) any remedy (re-performance, repair/replacement or refund). The Section 13 disclaimer does carve out the express warranties ("Except as expressly set forth herein ... except for the representations and warranties set forth in this Agreement"), so it does not swallow them; the gap is duration and remedy. We insert the missing warranty, period and remedy after p0041 as new clauses (xii)-(xiii) of Section 9(b), the smallest edit reaching the preferred position, with the 90-day fallback offered in the comment.

checks.name: warranty period ≥ 90 days or expressed in months/years

verification.notes: Deviation is correctly characterized: Section 9(b) as drafted warrants performance 'to industry standards' and freedom from utility-affecting errors but contains no professional/workmanlike services warranty, no conformance-to-documentation warranty with a stated duration, and no repair/replace/refund remedy; the rationale also correctly observes that the Section 13 disclaimer expressly carves out the Agreement's express warranties, so no edit to p0062 was needed. Redline is a valid, minimal insertion: new clauses (xii)-(xiii) hang correctly off the p0032 lead-in ('Kubient represents, warrants and covenants that:'), leave existing text untouched, and reach the preferred position (professional and workmanlike performance; 12 months for software deliverables and 90 days for services; repair, replacement, re-performance or refund at Vendor's option). Directionally pro-customer: the added warranty is additive and expressly non-exclusive ('in addition to, and does not limit, Customer's other rights and remedies'), so the new 90-day/12-month periods cannot be read to cut back the existing unlimited warranties in (ii) and (vi), and the remedy is not made an exclusive remedy. Comment is accurate, concise, in the required voice, cites the playbook position and offers the 90-day software fallback; deterministic checks (operation applies; period ≥ 90 days) are consistent with the text. Minor improvement (not disqualifying): the remedy sentence is drafted as covering breach of 'the warranties in this Section 9(b)' generally rather than only the new conformance warranty — narrowing it to clause (xiii) would remove any counterparty argument that it channels remedies for the IP, security and compliance warranties.

quote: Customer agrees to provide all reasonable and necessary access, support and cooperation for Kubient to provide the Services in a timely and effective manner.
rationale: Searches for "audit", "inspect", "records", "verif" and "books" return no hits, and a full read of the Agreement (single section, p0000–p0074) confirms Kubient has no audit, inspection or usage-verification right against The Associated Press and no right of direct or remote access to our systems. The only access obligation on us (p0001) is a cooperation covenant to enable Kubient to deliver the Services, and the fee mechanics in section 5 (p0023) impose no verification right or audit cost-shifting on us; indeed Kubient contracts with Advertisers and remits to us, so an "underpayment by Customer" audit mechanic is largely inapposite here. This rule is a protective limitation on Vendor audit rights, so genuine silence leaves us better off than the preferred position (once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, Vendor cost, no system access). Inserting an audit framework would be counterproductive, implicitly acknowledging an audit right and cost obligation that do not exist today, so no redline is proposed. If Kubient later proposes an audit clause, we should hold it to the preferred parameters and delete any system-access language.

verification.notes: audit frequency limited: failed Claimed status is 'compliant', and for a protective rule (limiting Vendor audit rights against us) genuine silence in the Agreement leaves the Customer better off than the preferred position, so no redline or counterparty comment is the correct output. The cited paragraphs support the compliance conclusion: p0001 imposes only a service-delivery cooperation/access covenant (not an audit, inspection or usage-verification right, and no direct or remote access to Customer systems), and p0023 sets out revenue-share and sequential-liability payment mechanics with no verification right or audit cost-shifting on Customer. The failed deterministic check ('audit frequency limited') is expected and non-probative here, since no audit clause exists to carry frequency/notice/cost parameters; inserting one would create a Vendor audit right that does not currently exist. Rationale correctly flags the residual watch-item (hold any future Kubient audit proposal to once per 12 months / 30 days' notice / independent auditor / Vendor cost, and strike system-access language) without proposing an unnecessary edit.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We added express prongs to Kubient's indemnity so it clearly covers allegations that the Service, Auction Platform or deliverables infringe third-party IP rights, as well as Kubient's breach of Law, Kubient-caused data incidents and its gross negligence or wilful misconduct. Our playbook requires the provider to stand behind third-party IP claims arising from its services on the face of the indemnity rather than only by implication through the Section 9(b)(i) warranty.

ops.text: (vi) any allegation that the Service, the Auction Platform or any deliverables provided by Kubient hereunder infringe, misappropriate or violate any patent, copyright, trademark, trade secret, publicity, privacy or other intellectual property or proprietary right of any third party; (vii) Kubient's breach of applicable Law; (viii) any unauthorized access to, or disclosure of, Customer's data or Confidential Information caused by Kubient; or (ix) Kubient's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.

proposal.summary: Add express IP infringement, breach of law, data breach and wilful misconduct prongs to Kubient's Section 10(a) indemnity.

quote: (iv) Kubient's breach of any representation or warranty under this Agreement or (v) the acts or omissions of Kubient or a third party hired by, employed, retained or under Kubient control with respect to Kubient's obligations hereunder.
rationale: Section 10(a) is a genuine Vendor-side indemnity in our favour (Services, Auction Platform, breach of representation or warranty, Kubient's and its subcontractors' acts or omissions), Section 11 supplies standard notice/control/cooperation procedure, and Section 7(a) carves indemnification out of the damages limitation so the indemnity is uncapped. However, the enumerated prongs (p0048-p0051) contain no express intellectual-property infringement trigger, nor express breach-of-law, Vendor-caused data incident or gross negligence/wilful misconduct triggers. IP claims are reached only indirectly, via the broad "Services"/"Auction Platform" wording or by first proving breach of the Section 9(b)(i) non-infringement warranty (p0033) - a route that lets Kubient argue an IP claim is outside the indemnity or requires proof of warranty breach before defence is owed. The playbook requires the provider to stand behind third-party IP claims on the face of the indemnity, so we add an express prong (vi) for IP infringement plus (vii) breach of Law, (viii) Kubient-caused unauthorised access to or disclosure of our data, and (ix) gross negligence or wilful misconduct. This is a clarifying addition consistent with warranties Kubient has already given (p0033, p0035, p0037, p0041) and should be uncontroversial; if Kubient resists, our fallback is the IP prong alone with the usual exclusions and procure/modify/replace/refund remedies. Spot-check on the reciprocal side: AP's Section 10(b) indemnity (p0052) runs wider than the preferred "Customer content / Customer breach of law" limit, extending to AP's unauthorised or inappropriate use of the Services and Auction Platform, breach of any representation or warranty, and the acts or omissions of AP and its contractors; we have left it untouched because it mirrors Kubient's own prongs and reopening it would invite reciprocal narrowing of the Vendor indemnity we are strengthening.

checks.name: vendor indemnity for IP infringement present

verification.notes: Status call is defensible: Section 10(a) is a real, uncapped Vendor indemnity with Section 11 procedure, but the enumerated prongs (p0048-p0051) contain no express IP-infringement, breach-of-law, data-incident or gross-negligence trigger, so IP claims are reached only through the broad 'Services'/'Auction Platform' wording or via the Section 9(b)(i) warranty - a real (if narrow) argument surface for Kubient. Redline is directionally correct and minimal: it appends prongs (vi)-(ix) to the existing Kubient indemnity list rather than rewriting the clause, tracks the model language (IP infringement allegation, breach of Law, Kubient-caused unauthorised access/disclosure, gross negligence/wilful misconduct), and leaves the existing prongs intact. Failed deterministic check ('vendor indemnity for IP infringement present') is not dispositive - the inserted text expressly indemnifies against 'any allegation that the Service, the Auction Platform or any deliverables ... infringe, misappropriate or violate any patent, copyright, trademark...', which satisfies the rule in substance; the regex miss is a phrasing variant. Comment is accurate, concise, in our voice, correctly cites the playbook position and the Section 9(b)(i) cross-reference, and does not misstate the contract. Caveat (not fatal): the preferred position also requires Customer's indemnity to stay narrow, and AP's Section 10(b) (p0052) is materially broader (unauthorised use, breach of any representation/warranty, acts/omissions of AP and its contractors). The finding acknowledges this and gives a tactical reason for leaving it, and the rule's redline guidance conditions narrowing on a one-sided clause, so the omission is documented rather than overlooked - but negotiators should revisit it if Kubient pushes back. Minor drafting nit: appending '(vi) ...' after a prong that already ends with 'or (v) ... hereunder.' creates a double conjunction/full-stop seam that should be tidied when the clause is engrossed.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement contains no insurance requirement, so we added our standard coverages (USD 1M/2M commercial general liability, USD 2M professional liability and USD 5M cyber liability, plus statutory workers' compensation) with certificates on request, given Kubient hosts the Auction Platform and collects and stores visitor data. If helpful, we can accept E&O of USD 1M and cyber of USD 2M as a fallback.

ops.text: Kubient shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the Term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; cyber and privacy liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000 covering Kubient's collection, maintenance, management and storage of Customer's and its visitors' data and Confidential Information; and workers' compensation insurance as required by applicable Law. Kubient shall provide certificates of insurance to Customer on request.

proposal.summary: Insert vendor insurance covenant (CGL, E&O, cyber) as new Section 14(j)

rationale: The Agreement has no insurance clause anywhere (searches for "insurance" return nothing; General Provisions in p0064-p0073 cover governing law, publicity, notices, force majeure and assignment only). Kubient is a services/hosting vendor that hosts the Auction Platform and, per its own warranty in p0035, collects, maintains and stores visitor information (data), so the playbook's preferred coverages apply. We inserted a new Section 14(j) requiring CGL of USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate, professional (E&O) liability of USD 2M, cyber/privacy liability of USD 5M and statutory workers' compensation, with certificates on request; the fallback of E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M is available if Kubient pushes back. The obligation binds the counterparty only.

verification.notes: Rule applies: the Agreement's General Provisions (p0063–p0073) contain no insurance clause, and Kubient is a hosting vendor that per p0035 collects, maintains and stores visitor data, so the preferred coverages are warranted. The inserted paragraph tracks the playbook model language (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, certificates on request) and adds only statutory workers' compensation, which the preferred position expressly contemplates; the obligation runs against Kubient only and no existing text is altered. Placement is appropriate — appended at the end of the General Provisions after the final subsection (i) — and the edit is additive, so the changed-character ratio is inherent to a missing-clause insert. Comment is accurate, concise, in our voice, cites the playbook position and offers the E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M fallback. Minor, non-blocking nits: the inserted paragraph omits the '(j)' subsection label referenced in the rationale, and it uses capitalized 'Term' and 'Law' which may not be defined terms in this Agreement — worth conforming at execution but neither changes substance or direction.
